## Solving Rosalind problems (bioinformatics)
Probabilities and python. 
<div>
Source: [Link to Rosalind](https://rosalind.info/problems/iprb/)

<h3 style="color:lightsteelblue"> What is the problem? </h3>
<p> 
Given: Three positive integers k, m and n,representing a population containing k+m+n organisms: k individuals are homozygous dominant for a factor (AA), m are heterozygous (Aa), and n are homozygous recessive (aa).

Return: The probability that two randomly selected mating organisms will produce an individual possessing a dominant allele (and thus displaying the dominant phenotype). Assume that any two organisms can mate.
</p>
<h3 style="color:lightsteelblue"> How to solve this problem? </h3>
<p>
We need to calculate the probability of getting one dominant allel, out of the given population. I struggle with abstract math, so I always think of an example, e.g. two German (AA), two Belgian (Aa) and two Dutch (aa) people meet in a bar. What needs to happen so they reproduce a kid with a dominant allel, when they mingle at random?
 (Lets say that the dominant allel stands for bad breath, we don't want this for our kids, but this is what they ask to calculate)
</p>

<h3 style="color:lightsteelblue"> Punnett square </h3>

<p>
- First we take a look at the possible outcomes with Punnet squares.  
The possible resulting kids are:

        German x Belgian (P(no A) = 0) (always smelly kid)
|   |   | A  | A  |
|---|---|----|----|
|   | A | AA | AA |
|   | a | Aa | Aa |

        German x Dutch 
|   |   | A  | A  |
|---|---|----|----|
|   | a | Aa | Aa|
|   | a | Aa | Aa |
- (P(no A) = 0) (always smelly kid) 
- As you can see, Germans are not favorable in this fictive story.

        Belgian x Belgian
|   |   | A  | a  |
|---|---|----|----|
|   | A | AA | Aa |
|   | a | aA | aa |
- Belgians have a P(no A = 0.25) of having a kid with no stinky breath. 

        Belgian x Dutch
|   |   | A  | a  |
|---|---|----|----|
|   | a | Aa | aa |
|   | a | Aa | aa |
- When the Dutch mix with someone from Belgium the P(no A = 0.5). So 50% chance of having a kid without a stinky breath.

        Dutch x Dutch
|   |   | a  | a  |
|---|---|----|----|
|   | a | aa | aa |
|   | a | aa | aa |
- When the Dutch have fun, the P(no A = 1). So always fresh teeth. 

So remember, to have a smelly breath, the kid has to have one A at least.
This is the same as calculating 1 - the probability of having no A at all (aa).
</p>

<p>
Now the question is, how to know what kids are possible with a given amount of parents. 
At the start, all adults are available. Let's say a Belgian makes the first move and the total amount of adults are 6. This means there is a 1/6 chance. Then we need another adult, so now there are 5 adults left for the Belgian to pick from. Remember, we want a kid without A, so we cannot go for a German partner. Se we can go for a Belgian one (1 remaining out of 5), or a Dutch (2 remaining out of 5). And then we can just do 1/6 * 1/5 OR 2/5 * P(no A). This needs to happen for each scenario (Dutchie making the first move etc.)

The P(no A) was calculated above, so now we can write python!
</p>
</div>


```{python}
with open("C:/Users/reino/OneDrive/Desktop/Portfolio2/posts/Mendel_Rosalind_Post/rosalind_iprb.txt") as new_file:
    #Read in file and split the numbers, than transform them into floats. 
    numbers = new_file.read().split()
    L = [float(i) for i in numbers]

G = L[0]
B = L[1]
D = L[2]

def dominant_probability(G, B, D):
    total = G + B + D
    # Calculate P(No A) when two Belgians are mingling:
    P_heterozygote = (B / total) * ((B - 1) / (total - 1)) * 0.25

    # Calculate P(No A) when two Dutchies are mingling:
    P_recessive = (D / total) * ((D - 1) / (total - 1)) * 1

    # Calculate P(No A) when A Belgian and a Dutch are mingling:
    P_hetero_recessive = ((B / total) * (D / (total - 1)) + (D / total) * (B / (total - 1))) * 0.5

    #Calculate probability of having no A (summing them):
    P_No_A = P_heterozygote + P_recessive + P_hetero_recessive

    # Calculate the Probability of having a dominant allel
    P_A = 1 - P_No_A
    print(round(P_A, 5))

dominant_probability(G, B, D)
```


<p>
Conclusion: in my dataset (G=30, B=21, D=30) the Probability of having a kid WITH a smelly breath (with a dominant allel) is 
P(at least one A =  0.75231). This means they need to start selling mouthwash and chewing gum in bars!
</p>
